deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivations. It is printed text from Riemann's posthumously published fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (edited by Henle, Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 1866/67; reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke). It does three things.

(1) Methodology. Riemann finishes the sentence begun on p.4. He must often contradict Helmholtz's conclusions, so he first states his respect for Helmholtz. In his view Helmholtz's merit lies in improving the empirical basis (Tonempfindungen), not in his theories of the ear's motions. He assumes the reader knows the anatomy of the ear and refers to the then recent third Lieferung of vol. II of Henle's Handbuch der Anatomie. He defines his task as explaining the psychophysical facts (the ear's performance) from these anatomical facts.

(2) Plan. The relevant parts are the tympanic cavity (Paukenhöhle) and the labyrinth (vestibule, semicircular canals, cochlea). For each part he will:
- infer from its structure what it contributes;
- then start from the task it must solve;
- derive the conditions needed for an adequate solution.

(3) Section 2, Paukenhöhle. It is long known that the middle-ear apparatus transmits the air pressure to the labyrinth fluid in amplified form. The conditions on this transmission come from two facts: the ear's fineness in perceiving Klang (timbre), and its great acuity, especially the 'unstunted' ear of the savage and the desert-dweller.

Definition: Klang is the property of sound independent of its strength and direction. Klang is transmitted with complete fidelity if the apparatus transfers the pressure change of the air at every instant (sentence continues on p.6) 'in constant ratio, enlarged', to the labyrinth fluid.

Modern restatement (mine): let p_air(t) and p_lab(t) be the pressure deviations. The fidelity condition is d p_lab/dt = k · d p_air/dt with k constant (k > 1). The middle ear then acts as an ideal linear, memoryless, distortionless pressure amplifier. Equivalently (anticipating p.6), log|d p_lab/dt| − log|d p_air/dt| = log k is constant. So the 'Klangcurve' log|p'(t)| is invariant up to an additive constant, i.e. it does not depend on sound strength.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page is qualitative. The physical claim that perfect timbre transmission requires an instantaneous constant pressure ratio is a sufficient condition (memoryless linear scaling), stronger than modern linear-systems fidelity. That weaker notion allows phase or frequency-dependent filtering, to which the ear is largely insensitive (Ohm/Helmholtz phase law). Riemann's stricter criterion reflects his rejection of Helmholtz's Fourier-based view and is not an error per se.

results.what: The middle-ear ossicular apparatus transmits air pressure to the labyrinth fluid in amplified form.
results.modern_name: Middle-ear impedance matching / pressure transformer (area ratio and lever action)
results.usually_credited_to: Helmholtz (Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen, 1868) and earlier anatomists/physiologists; Riemann says it was 'long recognized'

results.what: Fidelity criterion: timbre is preserved iff the instantaneous pressure change is transmitted in constant ratio (distortionless scaling).
results.modern_name: Distortionless (memoryless linear) transmission; scale invariance of timbre
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Mechanik des Ohres (1866, posth.), known published text

results.what: Methodological critique of Helmholtz and the analytic method in sensory physiology.
results.modern_name: Riemann's philosophy of science in sensory physiology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the printed, well-known posthumous paper 'Mechanik des Ohres' (in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke). It contains only methodological remarks and the qualitative statement of the middle ear's task, with no new mathematics.
